# 1 Maccabees Chapter 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_010_page_001.jpg

---

**1** In the one hundred and sixtieth year Alexander Epiphanes, the son of Antiochus, came up and took possession of Ptolemais, and they received him, and he reigned there.

**2** And Demetrius the king heard of it and gathered a very great army and went out to meet him in battle.

**3** And Demetrius sent a letter to Jonathan with words of peace, to exalt him.

**4** For he said: "Let us make haste to make peace with him before he makes peace with Alexander against us,

**5** for he will remember all the evils that we did against him and his brothers and against his nation."

**6** And he gave him authority to gather troops and to furnish arms, and that he should be his ally; and he commanded that the hostages in the citadel should be delivered to him.

**7** And Jonathan came to Jerusalem and read the letters in the hearing of all the people and of those in the citadel.

**8** And they were greatly afraid when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather troops.

**9** And those in the citadel delivered the hostages to Jonathan, and he gave them back to their parents.

**10** And Jonathan settled in Jerusalem and began to build and restore the city.

**11** And he commanded those doing the work to build the walls and Mount Zion round about with hewn stones for defense, and they did so.

**12** And the foreigners who were in the strongholds that Bacchides had built fled;

**13** each man left his place and went away to his own land.

**14** Only in Beth-zur did some of those who had forsaken the law and the commandments remain, for it was a refuge for them.

**15** And Alexander the king heard all the promises that Demetrius had sent to Jonathan; and they told him of the battles and the valiant deeds that Jonathan and his brothers had done, and of the toils they had endured.

**16** And he said: "Shall we find another man like him? And now let us make him our friend and ally."

**17** And he wrote a letter and sent it to him in these words:

**18** "King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.

**19** We have heard about you, that you are a mighty man of valor and worthy to be our friend.

**20** Now therefore we appoint you today to be the high priest of your nation, and you shall be called the king's friend — and he sent him a purple robe and a golden crown — and you shall have the king's interests at heart and maintain friendship with us."

**21** And Jonathan put on the holy garments in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the feast of tabernacles, and he gathered troops and provided arms in abundance.

**22** And Demetrius heard these things and was grieved, and he said:

**23** "What have we done, that Alexander has gotten ahead of us in making friendship with the Jews for support?

**24** I also will write to them words of encouragement and honor and gifts, that they may be with me."

**25** And he sent them a letter in these words: "King Demetrius to the Jewish nation, greetings.

**26** Since you have kept your agreements with us and continued in our friendship and have not gone over to our enemies, we have heard and are glad.

**27** And now continue to keep faith with us, and we will reward you well for the things you do for us.

**28** We will remit to you many remissions and give you gifts.

**29** And now I free you and remit to all the Jews the tribute and the salt-tax and the crown-levies,

**30** and instead of collecting the third of the grain and the half of the fruit of trees, which is my due to receive, I release them from this day and hereafter; I will not take them from the land of Judah nor from the three districts added from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.

**31** And Jerusalem and all its territory shall be holy and free from tithe and levy.

**32** And I remit my authority over the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, that he may establish in it whatever people he chooses who will guard it.

**33** And every soul of the Jews who has been carried captive from the land of Judah into all my kingdom, I will set free without payment; and let all their taxes be remitted, even the taxes on their cattle.

**34** And all the feasts and Sabbaths and new moons and appointed days, and three days before a feast and three days after a feast — let them all be days of exemption and freedom for all the Jews in my kingdom.

**35** And no one shall have authority to exact anything from them or to trouble any of them in any matter.

**36** And let thirty thousand of the Jews be enrolled in the king's forces and allowances be given to them as to all the king's forces, and let some of them be placed in the king's great strongholds,

**37** and some of them be appointed over the affairs of the kingdom that are matters of trust; and let their officers and leaders be from among themselves, and let them live by their own laws, as the king has commanded in the land of Judah.

**38** And the three districts that have been added to Judah from the country of Samaria — let them be added to Judah and reckoned to be under one rule, and not obey any other authority than the high priest.

**39** Ptolemais and its land I give as a gift to the sanctuary in Jerusalem for the expenses necessary for the sanctuary.

**40** And I give fifteen thousand shekels of silver every year from the king's revenues from the appropriate places.

**41** And all the surplus that the officials had not paid in as in the first years, from now on they shall give to the works of the temple.

**42** And in addition to this, the five thousand shekels of silver which they used to take from the income of the sanctuary each year — these too shall be released, for they belong to the priests who minister.

**43** And all who flee to the temple in Jerusalem and in all its territories, whatever their debt or their obligation — let them be released, and let all they have in my kingdom be free.

**44** And the cost of building and restoring the works of the sanctuary shall be paid from the king's revenues.

**45** And the cost of building the walls of Jerusalem and of fortifying it all around, and the cost of building the walls in Judah — these too shall be paid from the king's revenues."

**46** Now when Jonathan and the people heard these words, they gave no credence to them nor accepted them, for they remembered the great evil he had done in Israel, and how greatly he had afflicted them.

**47** And they were well-pleased with Alexander, because he had been the first to speak words of peace to them, and they were his allies all their days.

**48** And Alexander the king assembled a great army and encamped opposite Demetrius.

**49** And the two kings joined battle, and the army of Demetrius fled, and Alexander pursued him and overpowered them.

**50** And the battle was very fierce until the sun went down; and Demetrius fell on that day.

**51** And Alexander sent ambassadors to Ptolemy king of Egypt with words in these terms:

**52** "Seeing that I have returned to my kingdom and have taken my seat on the throne of my fathers, and have gotten the dominion, and have crushed Demetrius and gained control of our country —

**53** for I joined battle with him, and he and his army were crushed by us, and we sat down on the throne of his kingdom —

**54** and now let us establish friendship one with another, and give me now your daughter as a wife, and I will be your son-in-law and give gifts to you and to her worthy of you."

**55** And Ptolemy the king answered, saying: "Happy is the day on which you returned to the land of your fathers and sat on the throne of their kingdom.

**56** And now I will do as you have written; but meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I will become your father-in-law as you have said."

**57** And Ptolemy went out from Egypt, he and Cleopatra his daughter, and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.

**58** And Alexander the king met him, and he gave him Cleopatra his daughter; and their wedding was celebrated at Ptolemais with great pomp, as is the custom of kings.

**59** And Alexander the king wrote to Jonathan to come and meet him.

**60** And he went with pomp to Ptolemais and met the two kings and gave them and their friends silver and gold and many gifts, and found favor in their sight.

**61** And there gathered against him certain pestilent men of Israel, lawless men, to accuse him; but the king did not listen to them.

**62** And the king commanded that Jonathan's garments should be taken off and that he should be clothed in purple; and they did so.

**63** And the king made him sit by his side, and said to his governors: "Go with him into the midst of the city and make proclamation that no one shall accuse him of anything concerning any matter and let no one trouble him for any reason."

**64** And it came to pass, when his accusers saw the honor that was given to him according to the proclamation, and that he was clothed in purple, they all fled.

**65** And the king honored him and enrolled him among his chief friends and made him a general and a governor of the provinces.

**66** And Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with peace and gladness.

**67** In the one hundred and sixty-fifth year Demetrius the son of Demetrius came out of Crete into the land of his fathers.

**68** And Alexander the king heard about it and was greatly grieved, and returned to Antioch.

**69** And Demetrius appointed Apollonius as governor, who was over Coele-Syria, and he gathered a great force and encamped in Jamnia, and sent to Jonathan the high priest, saying:

**70** "You alone stand up against us; and I have become a laughingstock and a reproach because of you. Why do you exercise authority against us in the mountains?

**71** Now therefore if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us settle our strength there between us, for with me is the power of the cities.

**72** Ask and learn who I am and who the others are who are helping us; and they will tell you that you cannot stand before us, for your fathers were twice put to flight in their own land.

**73** And now you will not be able to withstand the cavalry and such a great force in the plain, where there is neither stone nor flint nor place to flee."

**74** Now when Jonathan heard the words of Apollonius, he was moved in his spirit and chose ten thousand men and went out from Jerusalem; and Simon his brother came to his aid.

**75** And he encamped against Joppa, but the men of the city shut him out, because the garrison of Apollonius was in Joppa; and they fought against it.

**76** And the men of the city were afraid and opened the gates, and Jonathan was master of Joppa.

**77** And Apollonius heard and mustered three thousand cavalry and a great army and marched to Azotus as if he was on his way through, while at the same time he was advancing into the plain, because he had a great number of cavalry and was putting confidence in them.

**78** And Jonathan pursued after him to Azotus, and the armies joined battle.

**79** And Apollonius had secretly left one thousand cavalry behind them.

**80** And Jonathan knew that there was an ambush behind him; they surrounded his army and shot arrows at the people from morning until evening.

**81** But the people stood firm, as Jonathan had commanded, while their horses grew weary.

**82** And Simon drew out his force and set it against the phalanx, for the cavalry had exhausted themselves, and they were crushed by him and fled.

**83** And the cavalry was scattered in the plain and they fled to Azotus and entered Beth-dagon the temple of their idol to find safety.

**84** And Jonathan burned Azotus and the cities round about it and took their spoils, and the temple of Dagon and those who had fled into it he burned with fire.

**85** And those who had fallen by the sword, together with those burned, were about eight thousand men.

**86** And Jonathan departed from there and encamped against Ashkelon, and the men of the city came out to meet him with great pomp.

**87** And Jonathan and those with him returned to Jerusalem with many spoils.

**88** And when Alexander the king heard these things, he added still more honor to Jonathan,

**89** and sent him a golden buckle, such as it is the custom to give to the king's kinsmen; and he gave him Ekron and all its territory for a possession.
